One-step overall water splitting system with (Ga₁–ₓZnₓ)(N₁–ₓOₓ) solid solution as photocatalyst, Rhodium–chromium mixed oxide nanoparticles (10–20 nm) as co-catalysts; Operational parameters: synthesis at 950°C for 0.25 h for sample A and 850°C for 15 h for sample B, visible light absorption with absorption edge at approximately 510 nm, band gap tuning from ~2.68 to 2.43 eV, 300 W xenon lamp or 450 W high-pressure mercury lamp as light source, photocatalyst powder (0.1 g or 0.3 g) in aqueous solution (100 mL or 370 mL) at pH 4.5 with H₂SO₄.
cool to room temperature while maintaining NH₃ atmosphere
calcine in air at 350 °C for 1 h
H₂:O₂ stoichiometric ratio maintained at 2:1 from the onset of the reaction, as confirmed by gas chromatography, indicating true overall water splitting
product origin confirmation supports water as the sole source of both gases

suppression of side reactions shows no evidence of undesired side reactions or byproduct formation was detected; the use of Rh–Cr mixed oxide co-catalyst was critical, as individual Rh or Cr oxides did not yield comparable activity
mechanistic controls confirm that the observed O₂ in standard OWS arises from water oxidation, not from catalyst decomposition or other sources
post-reaction characterization confirmed retention of the solid solution structure, composition, and optical properties (band gap and absorption edge unchanged)
morphological integrity revealed that Rh–Cr mixed oxide nanoparticles (10–20 nm) remained uniformly distributed on the catalyst surface post-reaction
H₂ evolution rate sustained over a 35-hour period, with a total evolved gas (H₂ + O₂) of 16.2 mmol, exceeding the catalyst amount (3.7 mmol) under visible-light irradiation
O₂ evolution tracked concurrently with H₂, maintaining the expected stoichiometry throughout the reaction
quantum efficiency (QE) 2.5% at 420–440 nm, and 3.0±0.2% at 400 nm
enhanced O₂ evolution QE for O₂ evolution increased to 51% at 420–440 nm in the presence of AgNO₃ as a sacrificial electron acceptor
long-term operation indicates photocatalyst maintained activity without noticeable degradation over repeated 35-hour runs, indicating robust photostability under continuous visible-light irradiation
mass balance validation confirmed accurate mass balance and reaction stoichiometry as the total evolved gas volume exceeded the catalyst amount
